Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the Lightning demo last week. Procurement and engineering at Kiln have a few follow-ups on how Redwood meters streaming outputs and how we should expect charges in the event of disconnects/retries. We’re preparing our SOW and want to make sure the cost model we budget matches reality. Two specific asks: 

1) If a streaming response is partially generated (client disconnects mid-response) — do we bill for the tokens generated server-side, for tokens acknowledged by the client, or something else?
2) If the client reconnects and retries (client-initiated, or network instability) and the model replays/duplicates a small prefix, how are retry duplicates billed? Is there a session resume window where duplicates are de-duplicated or not billed?

Attached is a short note from our engineering team (Kiln_RateRequest.pdf) with a couple of example scenarios. Procurement also asked for the hosted API baseline rate card so they can map to expected monthly usage. Can you loop in the right folks and share a clear billing example for each scenario (including if we should expect credits)?

Thanks — and we may propose a quick call if anything is ambiguous.

— Samantha

High-level answers up front so you can continue planning:
- Baseline billing: we bill on tokens generated by the model at the runtime level; for streaming responses that are sent as chunks we generally count the model-generated tokens, not client ACKs.
- Disconnects: if a streaming response is interrupted we charge for tokens generated up to the last committed send. There are edge cases for short-lived network blips where the session can resume without re-rendering tokens — Aditya will explain the resume window and de-dupe behavior.
- Retries/duplicates: can be handled several ways (resume, replay, or new generation). We offer a session-resume window (default 30s) where a resumed session will attempt to reuse the server-side KV/prefix and avoid re-generating duplicated tokens where possible; when exact duplication occurs, our runtime can suppress billing for replays under certain configurations — Marissa will outline typical commercial treatment.

Next steps: Aditya, can you provide concrete examples (token math) for the three scenarios Samantha attached? Marissa, can you add the rate card line items and a recommended credit approach we can put in the SOW?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon PT if you want to walk line-by-line.

Hi Samantha — Aditya here (solutions). I walked through the examples in Kiln_RateRequest.pdf and translated them into how our runtime meters tokens. Below are short, concrete examples and assumptions so you can plug numbers into budget models.

Assumptions: model emits tokens T1..Tn, streaming chunk boundaries are at token offsets, the server counts model-side token generation. Default session-resume window: 30s (configurable per-customer). Prefix caching (client-side prompts we cache) reduces re-generation in common flows.

Scenario A — Client disconnects mid-response (no resume):
- Client requests generation; model emits 120 tokens; after token 72 the client TCP connection drops and does not reconnect.
- Our runtime had generated and sent tokens 1..72; tokens 73..120 were not generated. Billing: charge for 72 model tokens. No automatic credit because generation beyond 72 never occurred.

Scenario B — Client disconnects and then reconnects within resume window, resumes from last token; exact resume (no re-generation):
- Same request; client disconnects after token 72; client reconnects within 25s and requests resume. Runtime reuses KV/prefix and resumes from token 73 — no duplicate generation. Billing: charge for 120 tokens (72 + 48 resumed). No duplicate billing.

Scenario C — Client reconnects and retries but triggers a small replay of the last N tokens (duplicate generation):
- Client disconnects after token 72; reconnects outside resume window or the client issues a new request that replays last 8 tokens to re-establish context; runtime regenerates tokens 65-120, resulting in duplicates for 65-72.
- Billing default: we bill for all model-generated tokens (so 120 tokens + 8 duplicated tokens = 128 tokens billed) because the runtime executed duplicate generation.
- Commercial/pricing mitigation: we offer a duplication suppression policy for customers on committed plans where we detect exact replay of the final K tokens and apply a credit for duplicated tokens over a monthly reconciliation window. This is not automatic for free-tier/spot-hosted usage.

Practical notes:
- If you expect flaky mobile or web clients, configure a short client-side debounce + server resume window to avoid replays.
- For long-polling/sever-sent events clients, prefer the resume behavior that avoids re-generation.

I can produce a CSV with token math for your sample QPS and mean response length if helpful.

Hi Samantha — Marissa from Billing. A few commercial rules we typically propose for enterprise customers and the examples you can use in the SOW. Attaching an Excel with worked examples.

Key commercial rules (recommended for SOW):
1) Metering unit: bill tokens generated by the model runtime. For streaming, that equates to tokens up to the last successfully emitted chunk.
2) Duplication credit policy: for customers on committed/monthly subscription tiers, we run a monthly reconciliation that detects exact duplicate token generation caused by retries/replays and apply credits for duplicated tokens when duplication > 1% of monthly tokens. Credits are issued as account adjustments in the following billing cycle.
3) Interrupt/short-blip grace: if a session disconnects and resumes within the configured resume window (default 30s), we will not bill duplicate tokens for exact resume operations. If the runtime needed to re-run an overlapping prefix, duplicated tokens are eligible for credit under rule (2) if the monthly threshold is met.

Worked example (use in SOW):
- Monthly committed volume: 300M tokens
- Week A incident: 5% of sessions experienced client reconnects that caused average duplicate generation of 12 tokens per affected session. Affected tokens = sessions_affected * 12. If duplicates represent 2% of monthly tokens (over threshold), we issue a credit for that duplicated portion equal to the token unit price.

Suggested SOW language (short):
"Redwood bills on model-generated tokens. For duplicate generation caused by client retries/replays, Redwood will perform a monthly reconciliation for customers with a committed plan. Duplicated tokens that exceed 1% of monthly usage will be credited to the customer at the applicable token rate."

Discounts/Rate card notes:
- Attached rate card has hosted API baseline rates. For Kiln’s estimated profile (starter projection you sent), we can extend a 15% volume discount at $200k/mo committed, and a 22% tier at $500k/mo. Discounts are applied to token-unit charges (not to infra surcharges or support addons).

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm if Kiln wants duplication-credit language in SOW.
- Samantha: if you can share an expected monthly token number or a QPS profile, we’ll produce a sample invoice and the monthly reconciliation clause verbatim for your contract team.

Thanks — happy to adjust thresholds for legal/tax if needed.
